issues.description: Storing a live FrameProcessor reference on a control frame is the wrong shape
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame now carries `service: FrameProcessor` — an entire processor object embedded in a dataclass frame. Frames travel through queues and get logged, copied, compared. Stuffing a stateful processor reference into a data-carrying control frame couples the frame to the live object graph and invites identity bugs (the equality check `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` is identity-by-default on dataclass without eq override, fine for now, but brittle the moment someone wraps or proxies the service). A stable service id or name on the frame would be the smaller, dumber, more correct shape.

issues.description: Forward reference to FrameProcessor as a string type with no import — works by accident
issues.detail: The dataclass field is annotated `service: "FrameProcessor"` but frames.py does not import FrameProcessor. That works only because dataclass doesn't resolve string annotations at runtime, and nobody calls `get_type_hints` on this. If anything in the codebase ever does (Pydantic-style validation, doc generation, serialization), this blows up. Either import FrameProcessor properly under TYPE_CHECKING, or — better — don't put a processor on the frame at all (see other comment).

issues.description: Behavior change buried in a 'rename' PR
issues.detail: Title says 'rename and add field'. The diff also flips STTService and the test mock from consuming the frame to pushing it downstream after handling. That's a real semantic change to the frame's lifecycle — every downstream processor now sees these requests where it never did before. Should have been called out as its own thing in the summary, and ideally landed as a separate patch from the rename. This is the THREE-PATCHES pattern: rename, add targeting field, change push-vs-consume semantics.

issues.description: Duplicated request-handling logic between STTService and the test mock
issues.detail: STTService and MockMetadataService now have the same pattern: on receiving the request frame, push metadata then forward the frame. If a second real service type ever needs this, you'll have three copies. A small base-class helper or a mixin method `handle_metadata_request` would eliminate the special case. Not blocking, but the kind of thing you fix now before it metastasizes.

issues.description: Suppression check no longer suppresses requests targeting other (inactive) services
issues.detail: Old code: any RequestMetadataFrame was swallowed at the switcher boundary. New code: only the one targeting the active service is swallowed; one targeting an inactive service falls through to downstream. In the current call path the switcher only ever emits a request for the service it just activated, so this is fine today. But the comment and the guard imply targeting is general — if anyone ever emits a request for a non-active service, it leaks downstream. Worth a one-line assertion or a comment nailing down the invariant.

review.summary: The patch does what it says: renames the frame, adds a service-targeting field, and changes the push-vs-consume semantics so the request frame can flow downstream. The rename is fine and the targeting idea is reasonable. What's wrong: putting a live FrameProcessor reference on a control-frame dataclass is the wrong shape — a stable id/name would be smaller and less coupled — and the string forward-reference works only because nobody's resolving type hints on this dataclass. The PR is also doing three things (rename, add field, change lifecycle); should have been three patches or at least called out clearly. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK. Swap `service: FrameProcessor` for an identifier, or properly TYPE_CHECKING-import the class, factor the duplicated request-handling helper, and it lands.
